column1: # Hand labels for iteration 10 of the engineering-role loop (issue #10).
# They label the 1000 rows sampled by iteration 9 in docs/measurements/engineering-role-2026-09-29.md.
# Labelled on 2026-09-22 from docs/engineering-role-criterion.md alone, at revision
# 29b1272245c5b0554f07f8907e87218b7756898b, over the bare cleaned titles, before any rule of the
# classifier was read.
# Labelled by a subagent denied the classifier's source, the iteration reports and the earlier
# label fixtures; it read the criterion and the sample and nothing else.
# This fixture is never regenerated: a session is not reproducible, so the labels are the artifact
# and not the process that made them.
# Families labelled under criterion rules a future revision might supersede:
# - Software-engineer heads carrying a hardware discipline marker: "Hardware Test Software
#   Engineer", "Software Engineer Hardware Test", "Radar Software Engineer", "Software Engineer
#   Motor Controls". Ruled OUT on step 4: the discipline marker beats the software qualifier, the
#   same reading the criterion gives FPGA/ASIC. A revision that reads "software engineer" as the
#   head and "hardware test" as the object of the software would flip all four to IN.
# - Engineer heads under a market marker naming a non-software industry, with no software
#   qualifier: "Trading Desk Operations Engineer", "Sports Operations Engineer", "Government
#   Project Engineer", "GTM Engineer". Ruled OUT on step 6, because step 6 fires before step 7
#   and "trading"/"sports"/"government"/"GTM" name who the work is for. A revision that let an
#   engineer head survive a market marker would make these domain_ambiguity instead.
# - Product management: "Product Manager II Search Experience", "Chief Product Officer", "Staff
#   Product Manager", "Product Manager Agentic AI". Ruled UNKNOWN/domain_ambiguity on the reading
#   that `manager` is not engineering-capable unless the modifier names engineering work itself,
#   so a software product area does not reach step 5. A revision that made a product area a
#   software qualifier under `manager` would turn this family IN; one that made `manager`
#   never-engineering would turn it OUT.
# - IT support and service desk: "Deskside Support", "Service Desk Analyst II", "IT Technician I
#   Remote", "End User Services Engineer". Ruled UNKNOWN/scope_ambiguity because the variants
#   split on Q3 — some read logs and configs, some reset passwords. Named tiers and named
#   technical domains were ruled IN instead ("L3 Support Analyst", "Network Support Engineer",
#   "Production Support Engineer", "Linux Desktop Support Engineer"), which is the line a revision
#   is most likely to move.
# - AI-training and annotation gigs: "Javascript Developers AI Training Tucson US" ruled IN
#   (a developer head with a software qualifier), "Biology Graduates AI Training Liverpool UK" and
#   "Portuguese Fluent Speakers AI Training BR" ruled OUT (the named credential is the discipline
#   being hired). A revision that read the whole family as annotation work would flip the first.
# - ERP and packaged-software functional roles: "SAP Warehouse Management Manager", "Oracle EBS
#   Projects Functional Lead Federal Financials G Invoicing", "Dynamics 365 F&O Functional Admin".
#   Ruled UNKNOWN/domain_ambiguity: the product is software but the title says "functional", and
#   Q2/Q3 split across configuration and development.
# - Analyst heads over non-software markets: "Financial Analyst Payments", "Underwriting Analyst",
#   "Valuations Analyst". Ruled UNKNOWN/domain_ambiguity under the criterion's own Treasury Analyst
#   ruling; a revision that narrowed `analyst` to domain-bound would make most of them OUT.
# id
# SUPERSEDED BY THE CRITERION REVISION OF 2026-09-24. The rows are never rewritten, but the
# families below were labelled before the criterion decided them, so a session pricing a
# candidate rule against the accumulated labels treats them as evidence-free rather than as
# costs:
#   - Managers: a manager over a technology noun (IT, Data, Security, Salesforce Manager) is now
#     scope_ambiguity, and a bare Engineering Manager, with or without a market marker, is now
#     domain_ambiguity.
#   - Technical Product Manager and Technical Program Manager are now IN; Technical Project
#     Manager is now domain_ambiguity.
#   - AI-training posts: the expertise named decides, and a post that names none is now
#     scope_ambiguity.
#   - Named enterprise packages (SAP, Salesforce, Oracle EBS, NetSuite, Workday) under consultant,
#     analyst or administrator are now scope_ambiguity.
#   - Reasons only, not states: a product title with no software qualifier is now
#     scope_ambiguity, and the two corpus reasons were redefined as "the domain is unclear" and
#     "the expertise is unclear".
